## Soft Metadata

> [!WARNING]
> **Tier 2 (community estimate)** — Soft Metadata below adapted from Wiley publisher pages and domain knowledge of European Association of Social Psychology (EASP) editorial culture. Submission practitioners are invited to upgrade individual claims to Tier 1 via `/ja-validate`. > **The core value of this entry.** OpenAlex cannot fill any of these — they require lived experience and community knowledge. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](../../../../CONTRIBUTING.md) for guidance.

### Epistemological & Political Leanings

| Dimension | Assessment |
|-----------|------------|
| **Cross-cultural friendliness** | Very High — EASP affiliated; European theoretical tradition |
| **Non-Western epistemology openness** | Medium-High — broader than US individualist focus |
| **Diversity topic receptiveness** | High — intergroup, prejudice, social identity well-represented |
| **Dominant theoretical tradition** | European social psychology — social identity theory (Tajfel, Turner), self-categorization, intergroup relations, collective action, social representations (Moscovici), discursive psychology |

### Framing Requirements

- **Mandatory framing?** Yes (strong)
- **If yes, what kind?** Manuscripts must demonstrate **European social-psychology theoretical contribution** — social identity, intergroup relations, collective phenomena, social representations.
- **Consequences of ignoring it**: Manuscripts misaligned with European tradition may face redirection.

## Strategic Notes

### Hard Blockers

- Manuscripts ignoring European social-psychology tradition
- AI use without disclosure per Wiley policy
- Pure US-individualist framings without intergroup / collective engagement

### Soft Tax

Low for European tradition. US authors may need to broaden theoretical engagement.

### Best Suited For

- Social identity theory empirical work
- Intergroup relations research
- Collective action and political psychology
- Social representations work
- Migration and cultural integration
- Discursive social psychology
- Cross-national European research

### Not Recommended For

- Pure US individualist social-cognition (consider JESP, PSPB)
- Pure personality research (consider EJP, J Personality)
- Pure applied without European theoretical engagement

### Rejection Fallback Chain

| Rank | Journal | Why this fallback works |
|------|---------|------------------------|
| 1 | [Personality and Social Psychology Bulletin](./personality-and-social-psychology-bulletin.md) | SPSP peer; if US-friendly reframe possible |
| 2 | [Journal of Experimental Social Psychology](./journal-of-experimental-social-psychology.md) | If experimental rigor emphasis |
| 3 | [British Journal of Social Psychology](./british-journal-of-social-psychology.md) | BPS-affiliated; UK / European social psychology |

**Reverse direction** *(optional)*: If your paper was rejected from JPSP as "too European-theoretical," EJSP is the natural EASP home.
